design: The loop's design (d4-whole-loop): section 2's rules R1 to R6, and Appendix B.4's families and listed exceptions.

read_values.spec.schema.json#/$defs/outcome/properti: the postmortem that a failed observe check writes
the release files, and the trunk when it lost the Spec

contained_ok.delegate-check.schema.json#/$defs/reason: `untested_acceptance` is its own reason, beside `untested`: two codes, not one value of two facts
contained_ok.item-types.schema.json#/$defs/type/prope: `typed_document` is a kind of document, one form
contained_ok.product-status.schema.json#/properties/f: `not_approved` is the negation of `approved`, one state
contained_ok.proposal.schema.json#/properties/go_no_g: `no_go` is the opposite of `go`, one decision
contained_ok.proposal.schema.json#/properties/qualifi: `no_go` is the opposite of `go`, one recommendation
contained_ok.retired-names.schema.json#/$defs/row/pro: `standard_id` is the id of a standard, one surface
contained_ok.status.schema.json#/$defs/branch_state: `intent_branch_missing` names the Intent's branch and `missing` the Spec's, one state each

several_questions.exploration.schema.json#/properties/time: minutes, a cost, or the day a spike ends

participle_flags.shared: a fact about an environment, that people share it: no one decided it
participle_flags.environment_shared: the same fact about an environment, as a rule matches it
participle_flags.reserved: an action reserved to a person: the risk rules' own mark, not an event
participle_flags.no_red: it mirrors the `--no-red` flag that sets it
participle_flags.untested: a runner's result: no test ran
participle_flags.recommended: the author's own mark on an option, which no person decides
participle_flags.locked: a lock that a parent config sets, shown by the config's own history
participle_flags.telemetry_opt_out: a fact about a third-party extension, as its own documentation says it

approval.means: a person's decision, with who and when

cancellation.means: a person's stop, with who, when, and why

qualified_kept.config.schema.json#/$defs/project_rule/p: BCP 14's `must`, `should`, and `may`: how firmly a project rule binds, which is no risk level
qualified_kept.config.schema.json#/properties/standards: the policy about standards is the config section itself, named for what it holds
qualified_kept.config.schema.json#/properties/locks/ite: the lock names that section by its own name
qualified_kept.config.schema.json#/properties/project/p: dark mode is a mode a screen has, the thing itself and no scope
qualified_kept.eval-claims.schema.json#/$defs/rules/add: a stop code is a named kind of stop, which the handoff note's schema owns
qualified_kept.evidence.schema.json#/properties/runner/: an id names what it identifies: the CI run
qualified_kept.lifecycles.schema.json#/$defs/thing/prop: a link to a row of the item types, so it names that kind of thing
qualified_kept.standard.schema.json#/properties/version: which version a project uses is a policy of its own, and `pinned` is one of its values

links.parent: the child names its parent by id
links.serves: an Intent or a product scope item names the outcome it serves
links.from: new work names what raised it
links.blocked_by: an Intent, a Spec, or a Task names what must finish before it starts
links.replaces: a decision names the earlier decision it replaces
links.covers: an Intent names the proposal needs it delivers
links.order: the intent order file ranks Intents: its own list, no parent's
links.spec: a postmortem names the Spec that repaired it, and `from` names the one that failed
links.specs: a proposal phase's trigger names the Specs whose merge starts the phase

child_list_places.common.schema.json#/$defs/phase/properti: an Intent's plan lists its planned Specs, and each Spec names its Intent in `parent`: the pair, until 1.1

ruled_out_statuses.common.schema.json#/$defs/test_status: test runner outcome in evidence (passed, failed, timeout, not_started), not a work-item lifecycle status
ruled_out_statuses.knowledge.schema.json#/$defs/status: URL check output of `aidd eval standards --online --json`, not a work-item lifecycle status
ruled_out_statuses.knowledge.schema.json#/$defs/release/pro: release probe output of `aidd eval standards --online --json`, not a work-item lifecycle status
ruled_out_statuses.standard-list.schema.json#/$defs/standar: catalog listing status of a library standard (replaced by K8), outside 4.1 and 8.1
ruled_out_statuses.standard.schema.json#/properties/status: catalog status of a library standard (replaced by K8), outside 4.1 and 8.1

other_enum_keys.decision: which way a decision went (`met`, `go`, `accepted`, `adopted`): a verdict about a thing, never a place in its life
other_enum_keys.state: what aidd reads about a branch or a file (`merged`, `approved`, `unreadable`), never a work item's status (8.1)
other_enum_keys.result: what a check showed (`passed`, `error`, `warning`): the outcome of one run, never a place in a work item's life
other_enum_keys.outcome: what a check or a delegate check came to (`eligible`, `defer`): one run's answer, never a place in a work item's life

not_decisions.announced_on: the day consumers were told of a deprecation: a fact about the product
not_decisions.assisted_by: the values of a commit's `Assisted-by` trailers: who helped write a commit, no decision
not_decisions.checked_by: who checked a source, such as a standard or a stack: a check of a fact, no decision
not_decisions.closed_by: who may close a thing (a key of `closers`), or who closes what a run opened: a rule of the loop, no decision
not_decisions.decided_by: the role that decides an action, a row of the roles' decision rights: a rule, with no decision made
not_decisions.finished_at: when a test run or an attempt ended
not_decisions.finished_on: the day a phase of a plan finished: a fact of the work
not_decisions.found_by: what finds a thing left open: a key of `finders`, a rule of the loop
not_decisions.measured_on: when a measure was taken: what the measure showed, never a person's decision about it
not_decisions.opened_by: who opens a thing, and how: a rule of the loop, no decision
not_decisions.read_by: the roles that read a document: a rule of the team, no decision
not_decisions.recorded_at: when a record was written: the record's own time
not_decisions.released_at: when a release reached its environment, in a release file: a fact of the delivery, written after the deploy
not_decisions.released_on: the day a release reached production: a fact of the delivery
not_decisions.restored_on: the day service came back: a fact of an incident
not_decisions.started_at: when a test run or an attempt began
not_decisions.suggested_by: who suggested work nobody asked for: where the draft came from, no decision
not_decisions.tested_on: the day a runbook was last tried: a fact about its test
not_decisions.written_by: the role that writes and keeps a document: a rule of the team, no decision

delegate_spec_approval.reason: a second form of `approval` on a Spec only, held by the delegate's record `{on_behalf_of, at, delegate_answer}` with no `by`

spec_report_or_allow.why_no_place: no object exists: the level of the risk rule is the hold, and R3 holds that a decision object is never required, so a Spec may have none
spec_report_or_allow.reason: a Spec approved at `report` or `allow`: no object at all, because the risk rule level is the hold

proposal_answer.reason: another party's answer as our person reports it, with free-text `by` and no `reason`; our decision is the `approval` that follows it

criterion_result.reason: a criterion's `result`: what a measure or a review showed; the decision is the `approval` inside it

scope_item_results.reason: a scope item's `results[]`: what a measure or a review showed; the decision is the product scope file's `approval` over it

revisions.reason: `revisions[]`: list of each time an approved Spec was sent back, each entry staying true; the decision is the yes to `spec.revise`

record_decision.why_no_place: its shape is the `types.decision` row of schemas/records.json, outside the `*.schema.json` files the walk reads; the record's own `by` and `recorded_at` are judged no decision
record_decision.reason: the record type `decision`: the agent's account of an ask and its reply outside git, with `question`, `answer`, and `recorded_at`
